terminal_objective.name: Polynomial proof-carrying SAT refuter
terminal_objective.quantification: For every fixed k and every sufficiently large encoding length n, refute every n-input circuit of size at most n^k.
terminal_objective.output: A legal CNF encoding F, the true SAT label b, a SAT assignment or fixed-system UNSAT proof pi, and a verified disagreement C(F) != b.
terminal_objective.total_cost: Polynomial in n plus the candidate-circuit encoding length.

proved_bridges.name: Certified refuter lower-bound bridge
proved_bridges.statement: A sound proof-carrying refuter against every circuit of size s(n) implies that SAT has no circuit family of size s(n).

proved_bridges.name: Certificate-preserving embedding transfer
proved_bridges.statement: A constructive refuter for f transfers to SAT when a polynomial certificate-preserving CNF embedding and a size-preserving circuit-composition theorem are supplied.

checks: rejection of corrupt labels or certificates
machine_checked_interface.scope: Interface validation only; no universal refuter is claimed.

located_bottleneck.name: NO_SHARING_REFUTER_AMPLIFICATION
located_bottleneck.statement: Current constructive gate-elimination lower bounds are linear. Reaching polynomial-size SAT circuits requires an amplification or magnification theorem that preserves explicit error extraction and certificates while controlling shared computation across copies.

active_hypotheses.name: Certified Refuter Amplification
active_hypotheses.next_gate: Give a sharing-aware amplification theorem with explicit runtime and counterexample extraction.

active_hypotheses.name: Certificate-Rich Restriction System
active_hypotheses.next_gate: Complete every simplification-discovered mismatch to a legal CNF with a generated SAT or UNSAT certificate.

active_hypotheses.name: Constructive Hardness Magnification
active_hypotheses.next_gate: Preserve refuter constructivity and proof-carrying labels through a magnification theorem.

forbidden_promotions: Multiplying a one-copy lower bound by the number of copies without a direct-sum theorem
Using an embedding whose composition causes uncontrolled circuit-size growth
Treating target-function evaluation as a free SAT or UNSAT oracle
Supplying an UNSAT verifier without a polynomial certificate finder
Promoting the finite XOR plumbing self-test to a general lower bound
claim_boundary: C031 does not construct the universal refuter, prove a superpolynomial circuit lower bound, or resolve P versus NP.
